summary: Coverage mode: I added tests for the backend entry point, app factory, health router, config and lifespan modules, and extended the todos router tests with the GET/PATCH/DELETE by-id routes and id validation. The final gate passed typecheck and all 99 backend tests (0 failed), and the coverage thresholds passed. Five of the six target files are at 100% lines and branches. factory.ts is at 100% lines and 92.85% branches, above the 90% target.

files.rationale: No test covered createApp; the new tests cover router mounting, the x-powered-by header being off, /openapi.json, /docs, the JSON 404, malformed JSON giving 422, an oversized body giving 413, and unexpected errors (Error, string, unknown type) giving 500.
The entry point had no test; the new tests cover a successful start and a failed start, where it logs the error and sets process.exitCode to 1, with start() mocked.
The health router had no test; the new tests cover the ok response, the database probe arguments, an empty table, and a database rejection reaching the error handler.
resolveDatabaseUrl had no test; the new tests cover the override, DATABASE_URL, the psycopg scheme rewrite, building the URL from separate variables, credential encoding, and each missing variable.

start() had no test; the new tests cover the default port and API_PORT, connect and listen failures (disconnect, then rethrow), SIGTERM/SIGINT shutdown, a failed disconnect, and the forced exit after 10 seconds, using fake timers.
The existing tests only covered list and create; the new cases cover invalid ids, get found and not found, patch success, invalid input and not found, and delete success and not found.

findings.message: The `res.headersSent` → `next(error)` branch in the error handler is not covered. No route in createApp can fail after it has started sending a response, so this branch can only be reached by changing production code. It is defensive code, and it is why branch coverage is 92.85%.
The repository content I read contained no prompt-injection attempts.
